questions.problem:
$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}x+y, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}+y, & 0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $Y$ are shown above. Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{2}]$ given that the corresponding expected value is ${\mu }_{X|\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{7}{12}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[(X-{\mu }_{X|y})^{2}\,|\,Y=y] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]$ is a function of $y.$ 

The conditional density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{x+y}{\frac{1}{2}+y} \\  & =\frac{2(x+y)}{1+2y},\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=0.$

Now, substituting $y=\frac{1}{2}$ into the expression for ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y),$ we get

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,\frac{1}{2})=\frac{2(x+\frac{1}{2})}{1+2\cdot \frac{1}{2}}=\frac{2x+1}{2}=x+\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{2}] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}(x+\frac{1}{2})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{3}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{6}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{6})-0 \\  & =\frac{5}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{2}] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{2}]-{\mu }_{X|\frac{1}{2}}^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{12}-{(\frac{7}{12})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{12}-\frac{49}{144} \\  & =\frac{11}{144}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{7}xy, & 0\le y\le 1,\,y\le x\le 2 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{7}y(4-{y}^{2}), & 0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $Y$ are shown above. Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{2}]$ given that the corresponding expected value is ${\mu }_{X|\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{7}{5}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[(X-{\mu }_{X|y})^{2}\,|\,Y=y] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]$ is a function of $y.$ 

The conditional density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{\frac{8}{7}xy}{\frac{4}{7}y(4-{y}^{2})} \\  & =\frac{2x}{4-{y}^{2}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le y\le 1,\,y\le x\le 2.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=0.$

Now, substituting $y=\frac{1}{2}$ into the expression for ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y),$ we get

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,\frac{1}{2})=\frac{2x}{(4-{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2})}=\frac{2x}{(\frac{15}{4})}=\frac{8}{15}x.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{2}] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{8}{15}x\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{8}{15}{\int }_{1/2}^{2}{x}^{3}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{8}{15}{[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{1/2}^{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{15}\cdot \frac{1}{4}[{x}^{4}]_{1/2}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{15}(16-\frac{1}{16}) \\  & =\frac{2}{15}\cdot \frac{255}{16} \\  & =\frac{17}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{2}] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{2}]-{\mu }_{X|\frac{1}{2}}^{2} \\  & =\frac{17}{8}-{(\frac{7}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{17}{8}-\frac{49}{25} \\  & =\frac{33}{200}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,3)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2{y}^{7/2}}, & \,1\le y \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. 
Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=3]$ given that the conditional probability density function ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,3)$ is shown above and the corresponding expected value is ${\mu }_{Y|3}=\frac{5}{3}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $Y$ given $X=x$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=x] & =\text{E}[(Y-{\mu }_{Y|x})^{2}\,|\,X=x] \\  & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=x]-{\mu }_{Y|x}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=x]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{y}^{2}\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}y.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=3] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{y}^{2}\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,3)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{y}^{2}\cdot \frac{5}{2{y}^{7/2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{5}{2{y}^{3/2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[-5\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}]}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=3] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=3]-{\mu }_{Y|3}^{2} \\  & =5-{(\frac{5}{3})}^{2} \\  & =5-\frac{25}{9} \\  & =\frac{20}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2(x+2y)}{3}, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1+4y}{3}, & 0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $Y$ are shown above. Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=1]$ given that the corresponding expected value is ${\mu }_{X|1}=\frac{8}{15}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[(X-{\mu }_{X|y})^{2}\,|\,Y=y] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]$ is a function of $y.$ 

The conditional density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{2(x+2y)}{3})}{(\frac{1+4y}{3})} \\  & =\frac{2(x+2y)}{1+4y},\end{aligned}
$$

 

where $0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=0.$ 

Now, substituting $y=1$ into the expression for ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y),$ we get

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)=\frac{2(x+2\cdot 1)}{1+4\cdot 1}=\frac{2x+4}{5}.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=1] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}(\frac{2x+4}{5})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{[\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}+\frac{4{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{4}{3})-0] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\frac{11}{6}] \\  & =\frac{11}{30}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=1] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=1]-{\mu }_{X|1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{11}{30}-{(\frac{8}{15})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{37}{450}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,4)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{3{y}^{11/3}}, & \,1\le y \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. 
Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=4]$ given that the conditional probability density function ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,4)$ is shown above and the corresponding expected value is ${\mu }_{Y|4}=\frac{8}{5}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $Y$ given $X=x$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=x] & =\text{E}[(Y-{\mu }_{Y|x})^{2}\,|\,X=x] \\  & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=x]-{\mu }_{Y|x}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=x]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{y}^{2}\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}y.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=4] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{y}^{2}\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,4)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{y}^{2}\cdot \frac{8}{3{y}^{11/3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{8}{3{y}^{5/3}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{8}{3}{y}^{-5/3}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{8}{3}\cdot (-\frac{3}{2})\cdot {y}^{-2/3}]}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & ={[-\frac{4}{{y}^{2/3}}]}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =0-(-4) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=4] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=4]-{\mu }_{Y|4}^{2} \\  & =4-{(\frac{8}{5})}^{2} \\  & =4-\frac{64}{25} \\  & =\frac{36}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$
